source: Written by Claude from general knowledge. Not checked against a reference.

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.seen: Orange, brown or yellow raised spots, mostly on the underside of the leaf, with pale marks above them.
diseases.plants: Leeks, garlic, broad beans, mint, hollyhocks, roses and pears.
diseases.when: Summer and autumn, worst in damp weather.
diseases.helps: Take off the affected leaves, give plants room for air to move, go easy on nitrogen feed and clear away dead leaves at the end of the season.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.seen: A white powdery coating on leaves and shoots, as if dusted with flour.
diseases.plants: Courgettes and squash, peas, apples, roses, gooseberries and grapes.
diseases.when: Late summer, when the soil is dry and the air humid.
diseases.helps: Water the roots in dry spells, mulch, thin crowded growth so air can move and take off the worst leaves.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.seen: Yellow patches with straight edges on top of the leaf, and a grey or purplish fuzz beneath them.
diseases.plants: Lettuce, onions, brassicas, peas and grapes.
diseases.when: Cool, wet weather.
diseases.helps: Space plants well, water at the base in the morning, take off affected leaves and move the crop next year.

diseases.name: Blight (late blight)
diseases.seen: Dark brown blotches that spread quickly across the leaves, with a pale edge and white fuzz beneath in damp air. Brown patches on tomato fruit. Potato tubers rot.
diseases.plants: Potatoes and tomatoes.
diseases.when: Warm, humid spells from midsummer.
diseases.helps: Cut down and remove blighted potato tops, grow tomatoes under cover, choose varieties that resist it and do not compost affected tubers.

diseases.name: Apple scab
diseases.seen: Dark, scabby spots on the fruit, which may crack, and olive-brown blotches on the leaves.
diseases.plants: Apples. Pears have a scab of their own that looks the same.
diseases.when: Wet springs and summers.
diseases.helps: Rake up fallen leaves in autumn, prune so air moves through the tree and choose varieties that resist it.

diseases.name: Apple canker
diseases.seen: A sunken patch of dead, cracked bark, often in rings round a bud or a wound. A branch dies beyond it once the patch goes all the way round.
diseases.plants: Apples and pears.
diseases.when: Seen at any time. It gets in through wounds and leaf scars.
diseases.helps: Cut back to healthy wood in dry weather and improve the drainage on wet ground.

diseases.name: Brown rot
diseases.seen: Fruit turns brown and soft with rings of cream spots on it. Shrivelled fruit hang on the tree through winter.
diseases.plants: Apples, pears, plums and cherries.
diseases.when: Summer and autumn. It gets in where the skin is broken.
diseases.helps: Pick off and throw away rotten and shrivelled fruit, from the tree and the ground.

diseases.name: Grey mould
diseases.seen: A fuzzy grey mould on soft fruit, flowers, leaves and stems.
diseases.plants: Strawberries, raspberries, grapes, tomatoes, lettuce and many plants under glass.
diseases.when: Cool, damp, still air.
diseases.helps: Clear dead and damaged growth, give plants room, ventilate a greenhouse and keep strawberries off the soil with straw.

diseases.name: Rose black spot
diseases.seen: Black or purple spots with a feathery edge on rose leaves. The leaf yellows around them and falls.
diseases.plants: Roses.
diseases.when: From spring onwards, worst when wet.
diseases.helps: Gather fallen leaves, prune out marked stems in spring and choose varieties that resist it.

diseases.name: Club root
diseases.seen: Roots swollen into knobs and clubs. The plant wilts on warm days and stays small.
diseases.plants: Cabbages, sprouts, cauliflower, swede, turnip, radish and wallflowers.
diseases.when: Summer. It stays in the soil for many years.
diseases.helps: Lime acid soil, improve the drainage, raise plants in pots before planting out, choose varieties that resist it and do not carry soil from an affected bed.

diseases.name: Peach leaf curl
diseases.seen: New leaves pucker, thicken and blister red, then turn white and fall.
diseases.plants: Peaches, nectarines and almonds.
diseases.when: Spring.
diseases.helps: Keep the rain off the tree from midwinter to late spring with a cover, pick off affected leaves, then feed and water so it grows fresh ones.

diseases.name: Chocolate spot
diseases.seen: Chocolate-brown spots on the leaves, stems and pods of broad beans, which can join into blotches.
diseases.plants: Broad beans.
diseases.when: Wet springs, and on plants sown in autumn.
diseases.helps: Space plants well, grow on well-drained soil and go easy on nitrogen feed.

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.seen: Seedlings fall over, pinched thin at the soil, sometimes with white fluff around them.
diseases.plants: Any seedlings in trays and pots.
diseases.when: Wet, warm, crowded sowings.
diseases.helps: Use clean pots and fresh compost, sow thinly, water sparingly and give the seedlings air.

diseases.name: Honey fungus
diseases.seen: A white sheet under the bark at the foot of the plant that smells of mushrooms, black bootlaces in the soil, honey-coloured toadstools in autumn, and a plant that dies back.
diseases.plants: Many trees and shrubs, among them apples, roses, privet and birch.
diseases.when: The toadstools show in autumn. The rest can be found all year.
diseases.helps: Dig out the affected plant with its stump and roots, and replant with something less prone to it.
diseases.note: The toadstools are not to be eaten on the strength of a drawing.

diseases.name: Sooty mould
diseases.seen: A black, sooty film on the leaves that wipes off.
diseases.plants: Any plant with aphids, whitefly or scale insects above the marked leaves.
diseases.when: Summer and autumn.
diseases.helps: Deal with the sap-sucking insects that drop the honeydew. The mould then weathers away, or can be wiped off.

diseases.name: Blossom end rot
diseases.cause: Not a disease: too little calcium reaching the fruit, from uneven watering
diseases.seen: A dark, sunken, leathery patch at the base of the fruit.
diseases.plants: Tomatoes, peppers, aubergines and courgettes.
diseases.when: Summer, most often in pots and growing bags.
diseases.helps: Water regularly so the compost never dries out, use larger pots and mulch.

diseases.name: Coral spot
diseases.seen: Small coral-pink or orange spots on dead twigs. It can spread from dead wood into live.
diseases.plants: Currants, figs, acers and many other woody plants.
diseases.when: Seen all year, clearest in damp weather.
diseases.helps: Cut out dead wood in dry weather, back to healthy growth, and do not leave prunings lying about.

diseases.name: Onion white rot
diseases.seen: Leaves yellow and wilt. At the base of the bulb is a white fluffy mould with tiny black dots in it.
diseases.plants: Onions, garlic and leeks.
diseases.when: Summer. It stays in the soil for many years.
diseases.helps: Lift and throw away affected plants, not on the compost heap. Do not grow onions there again for a long time, and do not carry soil from the bed.

diseases.name: Mosaic virus
diseases.seen: Leaves mottled in a patchwork of yellow and green. Growth is stunted and twisted and fruit may be marked.
diseases.plants: Courgettes, cucumbers, tomatoes and many others.
diseases.when: Any time in the growing season. Aphids and hands carry it from plant to plant.
diseases.helps: There is no cure. Take out affected plants, wash hands and tools after touching them and choose varieties that resist it.

diseases.name: Fireblight
diseases.seen: Blossom and shoots wilt and turn brown or black as if scorched. Shoot tips bend over like a crook, and the dead leaves hang on.
diseases.plants: Pears, apples, hawthorn, pyracantha and cotoneaster.
diseases.when: Late spring and summer, in warm wet weather.
diseases.helps: Cut out affected growth well below the damage, back to healthy wood, and clean the blades between cuts.
